pair.english: Do you have your ID card?
I want to withdraw some cash.
How much is the transfer fee?
I want to transfer money to this account.

lessons.culture: Many Yemenis change and send money through exchange shops (صِرَافَة) as well as banks, so you will often hear "أُصَرِّف" for changing money. Banks are closed on Fridays, and you need your ID card or passport to open an account.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I want to withdraw some cash."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal written Arabic; in Sana'a say "أَشْتِي أَسْحَب فُلُوس كَاش".

exercises.tip: "أَشْتِي" is "I want" in Sana'a; "تِشْتِي" is "you want".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I want to exchange some dollars."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "أَشْتِي أُصَرِّف شَوَيَّة دُولَار".

exercises.tip: "صَرَّف" is the everyday word for changing money; "بَدَّل" also works.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Here's your receipt." (to a man)
Which sentence means "Where's the ATM?"
Which sentence means "The machine swallowed my card"?
exercises.tip: "حَقِّي" means "mine" in Sana'a: "الكَرْت حَقِّي" is "my card".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "بِكَم / التَّحْوِيل / رُسُوم".
Put the words in order: "فِي / أَفْتَح / أَشْتِي / حِسَاب / البَنْك".

Complete: "_____ رُسُوم التَّحْوِيل؟" (How much is the transfer fee?)
The clerk asks: "مَعَك بِطَاقَتَك؟" Say yes, here it is.
You ask to withdraw cash and the clerk asks: "كَم تِشْتِي؟" Say fifty thousand riyals.

reply.english: At the end of the street.

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.arabic: ثَلَاث كِيلُو، وَالشَّحْن عِشْرِين أَلْف رِيَال
dialogue.transliteration: thalaath keeloo, wa ash-sha7n 3ishreen alf riyaal
dialogue.english: Three kilos, and the shipping is twenty thousand riyals.

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.english: Here you are. Do you want anything else?

response.english: At the end of the street.

pair.english: I want to send a parcel to my country.
How much does the parcel weigh?

response.english: Yes, this is the tracking number.

lessons.culture: At the post office the clerk weighs the parcel at the counter and sets the price by weight and country. House numbers are often missing, so people add a landmark or a PO box (صُنْدُوق بَرِيد) to the address, and many also use private courier offices for quick international parcels.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I want to send a parcel to my country."

too_formal.item: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُرْسِلَ طَرْدًا إِلَى بَلَدِي
too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "أَشْتِي أَبْعَث طَرْد لِبَلَدِي".

exercises.tip: "بَعَث" is the everyday word for "send"; "أَرْسَل" is more formal.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "How much is the shipping?"
Translate: "Where's the mailbox?"
exercises.tip: "ق" in "صُنْدُوق" is said g in Sana'a.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Write the address here" (to a man)?
Which sentence asks how long it takes to arrive?
Put the words in order: "كَم / الطَّرْد / وَزْن".
Put the words in order: "أَبْعَثه / بَرِيد / أَشْتِي / مُسَجَّل".
Complete: "أَشْتِي أَبْعَث _____ لِبَلَدِي." (I want to send a parcel to my country.)
Complete: "فِين _____ البَرِيد؟" (Where is the mailbox?)
exercises.tip: "صُنْدُوق" is a box; the post office itself is "مَكْتَب البَرِيد".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "فِين مَكْتَب البَرِيد؟" Say: at the end of the street.
The clerk asks: "تِشْتِي شِي ثَانِي؟" Say: no thanks, that's all.

How many gigabytes do you want?

pair.english: Can the service be activated today?
What is my new phone number?

response.english: This is your number, save it.

lessons.culture: SIM cards are sold in phone shops and kiosks, and the seller usually registers the line with your ID card or passport. Most people use prepaid balance that they top up, and internet packages are sold by the month. For a mobile you will hear both تِلِفُون and جَوَّال, and phone shops also repair screens and sell chargers.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I want to buy a SIM card."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "أَشْتِي أَشْتَرِي شَرِيحَة".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "My phone screen is broken."
Translate: "What is my new phone number?"

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "إِيش رَقْم تِلِفُونِي الجَدِيد؟".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I want to top up my balance"?
exercises.tip: "شَحَن رَصِيد" is to top up; "شَاحِن" is a charger.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "The signal is weak here"?
Put the words in order: "بِكَم / هَذِي / البَاقَة".
Put the words in order: "أَشْتِي / شَاحِن / جَدِيد".
Complete: "أَشْتِي أَشْحَن _____." (I want to top up my balance.)
exercises.tip: "رَصِيد" is the balance on your line.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الشَّبَكَة _____ هُنَا." (The signal is weak here.)
The seller asks: "كَم جِيجَا تِشْتِي؟" Say ten gigabytes.
A customer asks: "هَذَا التِّلِفُون يَشْتَغِل بِشَرِيحَتَين؟" You are the seller. Say yes, it has two slots.

reply.arabic: مَا فِيش مُشْكِلَة، تَكَلَّم عَلَى مَهَلَك

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.english: Hello, I want the ambulance!

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.english: I'll go out now.

response.arabic: مَا فِيش مُشْكِلَة، تَكَلَّم عَلَى مَهَلَك

lessons.culture: Emergency numbers differ from country to country, so find out the local numbers before you need them. In Yemen the fire service is called الدِّفَاع المَدَنِي (civil defence). Say where you are first, speak slowly, and stay on the line so help can find you.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Call an ambulance." (to a man)
Translate: "I need a doctor."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "أَنَا مُحْتَاج دُكْتُور".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I don't speak Arabic very well."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "مَا أَتَكَلَّمش عَرَبِي قَوِي".

exercises.tip: "مَا ... ش" wraps the verb for "don't"; "قَوِي" after it means "very".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "There is a fire"?
exercises.tip: "فِيه" is "there is"; "ق" in "حَرِيق" is said g.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Where is the nearest hospital?"
Put the words in order: "إِيش / رَقْم / الطَّوَارِئ".
Put the words in order: "فِين / أَقْرَب / مُسْتَشْفَى".
Complete: "_____ حَرِيق." (There is a fire.)
Complete: "خَلِّك عَلَى _____." (Stay on the line.)
You shout "سَاعِدُونِي!" and someone asks: "إِيش صَار؟" Say: I need a doctor.
You ask for the police and the operator asks: "فِين أَنْتَ؟" Say: this is the address.
exercises.tip: Give the address first, then stay on the line.

reply.english: We'll take you to the hospital.

response.english: We'll take you to the hospital.

pair.english: I want a report from the police.

lessons.culture: After a road accident people stay calm and help anyone hurt without moving them. The traffic police (المُرُور) usually come and write a report, which the insurance company asks for. To someone who has come through safely you say "الحَمْدُ لِلَّه عَلَى السَّلَامَة".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "There has been an accident."
Translate: "Do not move." (to a man)

too_formal.feedback: This is the formal form; in Sana'a the verb after "لَا" takes "ـش".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I want a report from the police."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "أَشْتِي تَقْرِير مِن الشُّرْطَة".

exercises.tip: "تَقْرِير" is a report; "ق" is said g.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Bring the first aid kit"?
exercises.tip: "جَاب" is to bring; "شَنْطَة" is a bag.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "My leg hurts"?
exercises.tip: "رِجْل" is a leg and "تُوجِعْنِي" is "it hurts me".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "رِجْلِي / تُوجِعْنِي".
Put the words in order: "اِتَّصِل / بِأَهْلِي / لَوْ سَمَحْت".
Complete: "فِيه حَد _____؟" (Is anyone hurt?)
Complete: "هَذِي بِطَاقَة _____ حَقِّي." (This is my insurance card.)
A passer-by asks: "فِيه حَد مُصَاب؟" Say yes, one person.
Someone asks: "أَنْتَ بِخَيْر؟" Say you are fine, thank Allah.
exercises.tip: "الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه" is the same in every dialect.

phrases.arabic: أَعْلِن عَنْه بِمُكَبِّر الصَّوْت لَوْ سَمَحْت

reply.english: No, I haven't seen him, sorry.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you.

dialogue.speaker: حمزة
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you, what is wrong?

pair.english: He is wearing a red shirt.
Where did you see him last?

lessons.culture: In a crowded place such as a market, go straight to a security guard or the shopkeepers nearby, who will call out the child's description. In Sana'a a child is a جَاهِل and children are جُهَّال. Keep a recent photo on your phone, and say "الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه" when the child is found.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "My child is lost."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; in Sana'a say "جَاهِلِي ضَايِع".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "He is five years old."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "عُمْرُه خَمْس سِنِين".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Have you seen a small child?"

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "شُفْت جَاهِل صَغِير؟".

exercises.tip: "شُفْت" is "did you see" when said as a question.

challenge.title: A morning of errands
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines in Sana'ani Arabic. You withdraw cash at the bank, ask where the post office is, ask the cost of sending a parcel, and top up your phone balance. Use at least 8 phrases from Unit 19.
required_elements: A request at the bank with أَشْتِي أَسْحَب فُلُوس كَاش.
A question about the post office with فِين.
A question about a price with بِكَم.
A request to top up the phone balance with أَشْتِي أَشْحَن رَصِيد.
A polite word such as لَوْ سَمَحْت or شُكْرًا.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَشْتِي أَسْحَب فُلُوس كَاش.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I want to withdraw some cash.

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام، حَيَّا بِك. كَم تِشْتِي؟
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you, welcome. How much do you want?

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.arabic: مِيَّة أَلْف رِيَال. وَفِين مَكْتَب البَرِيد لَوْ سَمَحْت؟
dialogue.transliteration: miyya alf riyaal. wa feen maktab al-bareed law sama7t?
dialogue.english: A hundred thousand riyals. And where is the post office, please?

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.arabic: فِي آخِر الشَّارِع، جَنْب مَحَلّ التِّلِفُونَات.
dialogue.transliteration: fi aakhir ash-shaari3, janb ma7all at-tilifoonaat.
dialogue.english: At the end of the street, next to the phone shop.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.english: I want to send a parcel. How much is the shipping?

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.english: Twenty thousand riyals.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.english: And I also want to top up my balance.

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.english: Here you are. How much do you want to add?

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.english: Thank you. May Allah reward you with good.

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.english: And you too.
